title: How can 16 tiles make a figure with exactly one or two fold lines?
description: Sixteen coloured tiles are laid in a square of four tiles by four tiles. A left half and its mirror picture give a figure with exactly one line of symmetry, and a filled quarter with two mirror pictures gives a figure with exactly two. Each figure is checked by folding, including the slanting folds that must fail.
teaching_notes: One idea: the mirror picture across a line makes that line a line of symmetry, and the other folds are checked so that the count is exact. Watch for students who think a figure can have only one line of symmetry, or who forget to test the slanting folds.

video_script.why: The child builds two figures from sixteen tiles by taking mirror pictures, and checks by folding that each has exactly the number of lines wanted.
video_script.substitution: Sixteen of the book's coloured tiles, laid in a square of four tiles by four tiles.
video_script.anchor: sixteen square tiles from the book, each cut by a slanting line into a blue triangle and a yellow triangle, laid in a square of four tiles by four tiles
video_script.payoff_line: Both figures can be made with sixteen tiles

final_answer.value: a 4 by 4 arrangement with exactly one fold line, and another with exactly two fold lines
final_answer.spoken: a figure of four tiles by four tiles with exactly one fold line, and another figure with exactly two fold lines

hold_back: another with exactly two fold lines
never_show: a figure with a third or fourth fold line shown as having exactly two
a mirror picture drawn without flipping the tiles
maths_rules: 16 tiles = 4 by 4; each half is 4 rows by 2 columns = 8 tiles; each quarter is 2 by 2 = 4 tiles
tile code: the corner where the blue triangle has its right angle: TL top left, TR top right, BL bottom left, BR bottom right
mirror across the vertical line swaps TL with TR and BL with BR; mirror across the horizontal line swaps TL with BL and TR with BR
figure with exactly 1 line, rows from the top: TL TL TR TR / BL BL BR BR / BL BL BR BR / BL BL BR BR

vertical fold matches (left half is mirrored); horizontal fold: row 1 matches row 4 but row 2 does not match row 3 (BL would need to land on TL); slanting folds: the tile in row 1 column 2 (TL) lands on row 2 column 1 (BL) and does not match; so exactly 1 line

figure with exactly 2 lines, rows from the top: TL TL TR TR / BL TL TR BR / TL BL BR TR / BL BL BR BR (top left quarter TL TL / BL TL, mirrored across the vertical line, then the top half mirrored across the horizontal line)

vertical and horizontal folds match; slanting folds: the tile in row 1 column 2 (TL) lands on row 2 column 1 (BL) and does not match, and the tile in row 1 column 2 (TL) lands on row 3 column 4 (TR) on the other slanting fold and does not match; so exactly 2 lines
slip: a figure can have more than one line of symmetry; and a figure must not have extra lines beyond the number wanted
video_script.design: One idea: take the mirror picture across a line, then check every other fold. One square of four by four tiles, built twice, with the middle lines red and the flip arrows teal.
